items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' anywhere. Once the call turned from a compliment call into a live quote ('but to move from storage storage two people is still what $100 per person'), Chris never reset the frame — no 'let me grab a few details and walk you through pricing, takes about ten minutes.' The whole back half of the call wandered because no roadmap was ever set.

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — the single largest miss on this call. The customer OPENED with a damage report ('outside of knocking one table over and a little chip on it'), then volunteered that the items are antiques ('cause they were antiques and stuff'), then disclosed a break-in with an open insurance claim. Three separate openings for the $2,000 coverage pitch, and Chris took none of them.

Meet Your Mover never mentioned, despite the customer specifically asking for the crew by name twice ('would you say Nick or somebody cause he knows what's in that storage') — she was literally asking for mover continuity, which is the differentiator's exact selling point.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.

No 'pricing is super simple' framing, no what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools), and no 'no hidden fees' pitch — on a call where the customer was actively doing worth-it math out loud ('now I got to figure out is it's worth it').

Disassembly / reassembly never mentioned even though the stated inventory includes 'chairs from a table, there's a card table, there's a couple of curio cabinets' and a dresser — items where assembly time is a real variable.
No 'no deposit required' mention. The customer was hesitating purely on cost-certainty; 'there's no deposit to hold the date' was the exact unlock available and was never said.
No email handoff at all — no confirmation email, no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections.' The call ended on a verbal 'I'll ask him' with nothing in writing on either side.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'

Clock explanation was half-delivered: the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments were both stated correctly, but 'clock starts on-site when the contract opens' was never said, and there was no sense-check ('does that make sense?') after a fairly dense pricing block.

Entire Save Your Ass section skipped. No prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples (loose items in drawers of the dresser and nightstands, contents of the curio cabinets), no sense-check close. This was the highest-leverage section available: the customer's only objection was whether the job clears the minimum, and prep advice is what actually shortens it.

No Sparefoot / storage referral, despite the customer explicitly complaining about storage costs — 'By the time I pay the storages I probably could buy a new house right' — and running at least two units she is trying to consolidate.
Customer's name never used once in the entire call. She introduced herself in the second line ('Hey Chris, it's Dina Shaw') and Chris never said 'Dina' at any point.

Specialty-item handling never addressed as an estimate variable — two antique couches, two curio cabinets, and a glass-top table are the exact items that slow a crew down, and Chris listed them back as inventory ('if there's a couple of Curio cabinets, couches, chairs, dresser') without tying any of them to time.

Walk distance never asked. He got the floor ('both on the first floor') but never asked how far the units are from the loading area at either Public Storage, which on a self-storage job is often the biggest time driver.
Access concerns never asked — gate codes, hours, and loading-dock access at two Public Storage facilities, none of it captured on a job he was offering to book.
Special considerations (long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns) never probed.

Packing needs never asked. He asked inventory ('Other boxes or miscellaneous items or just furniture') but never whether the antiques need wrap or pack service — on a load she had already told him got damaged once.

Moving stressors never asked, and a volunteered one went unworked. She disclosed 'they broke into the unit and stole some stuff out of it... they're brushing it for fingerprints' and the response was 'No Jeez. Okay. Well I mean ultimately' — then straight back to the estimate. No empathy, no offer to help locate the missing table glass during the move, no coverage tie-in.

Estimate was never owned. Chris deferred the number to an absent crew lead three separate times ('Nick is off today', 'I'll definitely ask him', 'I just don't know when I'll be able to talk to him'), which is what left a ready-to-book repeat customer unbooked.
Truck count never stated — he landed on 'it sounds like we're a two man team could do it' but never confirmed one truck.

Delivery was fragmented on the numbers. The rate came out as 'anywhere from like, one to one per hour for movers of 22 for two to like $222', then 'It's $102 The u will be $102 per hour for movers. The $2,204 per hour for three minutes or two maintain', and the range as 'anywhere from the minimum to like 45 hours.' Even allowing for transcription noise, the customer had to ask the price twice ('And how much is it again to move from?').
top_strength: Two things genuinely worked here. First, the relationship. This is a repeat customer who called unprompted to praise the crew, and Chris handled that with real, specific warmth — he named the movers rather than giving a generic thank-you ('we had a pretty good crew, Nick's been with us a long time, Adrian other guy not as long'), promised to pass it on ('Awesome, yeah, I'll definitely let them know, thank you for calling and telling us'), and recognized her loyalty out loud ('we can work with you since you've moved us so many times'). He also remembered her prior job ('I think I remember your last one'). That is the kind of rapport that produces this call in the first place. Second, the cost math was concrete and correct. He gave the day-of-week tiers unprompted and accurately — 'The cheapest days are Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday is the highest and then Sunday Monday are kind of between those' — proactively supplied the drive time ('It's about nineteen minutes away'), and then did the arithmetic for her in both directions rather than making her do it: 'if it took four hours total, your total cost would just be... $204 an hour times four. So it'd be $816', and 'If it took a minimum two and a half hours or less it'd be $510 total.' Both figures check out. Ending a price conversation with a real dollar total instead of an hourly rate is exactly right and most reps do not do it.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: Chris had a loyal repeat customer, on the phone, asking to be sold, with a small well-understood job at two addresses he already had — and he handed the close to a mover who was off work that day. Her only hesitation was whether the job clears the 2.5-hour minimum, and she told him the answer to that ('there's not much left in there. Mostly it's like chairs from a table, there's a card table, there's a couple of curio cabinets... two small couches antique couches and a dresser'). He had the inventory, the dimensions (10x20), the floors (both first), and the drive time (19 minutes). The line he needed, right after 'it sounds like we're a two man team could do it', was: 'Dina, based on what you've described I'm comfortable putting two movers and a truck on it for a three-hour window — that's $612 at the Tuesday rate, and if they finish at the two-and-a-half-hour minimum it drops to $510. There's no deposit, so let's lock Tuesday the 9th right now and I'll still check with Nick and email you if anything changes.' That books the job today and keeps the Nick follow-up as a courtesy instead of a blocker. Second priority, and it is close behind: this call opened with a damage report on antique furniture and later included a storage break-in with an open insurance claim, and No Worries Damage Coverage was never said out loud. The line was 'That's exactly what our No Worries coverage is for — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse accidental damage, which is why you got that call this morning instead of chasing us for weeks like your last company.' She handed him that comparison herself ('I've had other moving companies destroy my stuff and he can't get a hold of them'). Turning her own words into the differentiator is free and he walked past it. Third, use her name — zero uses in a 13-minute call with a repeat customer who opened by introducing herself. Two business items for Amanda, separate from the score: (1) Chris verbally offered to waive the 2.5-hour minimum — 'we could lower the minimum in your case' — which is a pricing exception given on the fly with no dollar figure, no approval trail, and nothing in writing, and it is now something this customer expects; worth confirming whether BMs have that latitude. (2) There are two open service issues on this account with no visible ownership: the chipped table from the 9/3 move, and the missing glass top from the broken-into unit that she believes Einstein was going to help locate ('we cause you were going to come and move this stuff around and find the glass'). Neither was confirmed as logged on the call.
phone_presence_notes: Real warmth and a genuine relationship carried the call — he named the crew and recognized her loyalty, and she stayed happy to the end ('well thank you very much, I appreciate it') — but the language was heavily disfluent, the numbers came out garbled enough that she had to ask the price twice, and two emotional beats landed poorly: a damage report answered with 'Oh, that's good. Awesome' and a burglary answered with 'No Jeez. Okay. Well I mean ultimately.'
audio_review_reason: The quoted rate is unreadable in the transcript at the moments that matter most — 'anywhere from like, one to one per hour for movers of 22 for two to like $222' and 'It's $102 The u will be $102 per hour for movers. The $2,204 per hour for three minutes or two maintain' — so it cannot be determined from text whether Chris actually misquoted the hourly rate on a live pricing call, or whether it is ASR noise on a correct $102/mover/hour. The customer asking 'And how much is it again to move from?' suggests she did not hear it cleanly either. Audio also needed to judge tone on the burglary disclosure.
